title: Giving Nuanced Advice and Setting Boundaries
summary: Exploring needs, offering non-directive advice, and communicating personal or professional limits.
whyItMatters: Supportive conversations preserve the other person's agency while making limits, risks, and options clear.

mentalModel.title: Understand before advising
mentalModel.content: Clarify what the person wants from the conversation and what they have already tried.

mentalModel.title: Care and limits can coexist
mentalModel.content: A boundary describes what you can do, what you cannot do, and which alternative support may be available.

ruleBlocks.title: Reflect and clarify
ruleBlocks.content: Summarize the concern, ask open questions, and check whether advice is welcome.

ruleBlocks.title: Offer options, not diagnoses
ruleBlocks.content: Use tentative language, compare consequences, and leave the decision with the person.

ruleBlocks.title: State boundaries concretely
ruleBlocks.content: Use first-person language, name the limit, explain relevant consequences, and propose a workable next step.

tables.title: Support and Boundary Toolkit
rows: Möchtest du, dass ich nur zuhöre, oder wünschst du dir einen Rat?
Ich kann ..., aber ich kann nicht ...
Dabei wäre professionelle Unterstützung möglicherweise hilfreicher.

examples.de: Möchtest du zuerst erzählen, was dich am meisten belastet, oder sollen wir direkt nach Möglichkeiten suchen?
examples.en: Would you first like to explain what is weighing on you most, or should we look directly for options?

examples.de: Eine Möglichkeit wäre, die Aufgaben vorübergehend neu zu priorisieren; entscheiden musst du das natürlich selbst.
examples.en: One option would be to reprioritize the tasks temporarily; the decision is of course yours.

examples.de: Ich kann heute eine Stunde zuhören, aber ich kann keine ständige Erreichbarkeit versprechen.
examples.en: I can listen for an hour today, but I cannot promise constant availability.

commonMistakes.wrong: Give immediate solutions before understanding the need.
commonMistakes.correct: Ask whether the person wants listening, information, or advice.

commonMistakes.wrong: Use a vague boundary and expect others to infer it.
commonMistakes.correct: State the concrete limit and available alternative.
commonMistakes.reason: Clarity reduces resentment and repeated negotiation.

comparisons.summary: The theme supplies a non-reductive view of stress, support, and professional care.
